items.title: Banks Preparing for Aftermath of Unprecedented Catastrophe Caused by AI: "You can't stop it."
items.content:
Doomsaying about the coming AI apocalypse is no longer relegated to outbursts from a few tech billionaires .

Now, the major American banks whose policies dictate the flow of capital throughout the world are starting to worry about rogue AI, preparing contingency plans for the “day after” a theoretical AI-driven catastrophe.

That’s according to new reporting from Axios , which notes that banks are preparing for the worst as they experience a huge rise in AI agent activity on behalf of individual customers.

The main worry seems to be an influx of financial activity driven by autonomous AI agents, which have been authorized to access bank accounts by their human users. In some cases, as Axios noted previously , those agents are making moves that haven’t explicitly been prompted by humans — a few even going so far as to contact call centers on behalf of their users, without being instructed to do so.

That’s become a major liability for top banks like Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo, which are scrambling to implement security procedures and policy updates to get ahead of the AI swarm.

Failing to stay on top of emerging risks, some experts say, could result in financial catastrophe. As chief economist at the Apollo wealth management firm Torsten Slok explained in a late September brief , AI agents operating under instructions to “optimize the return” on their users’ money could mean banks “lose a large share of the cheap deposits they rely on to make loans, which would be a problem for the entire financial system.”

As skeevy as that admission is, there’s plenty of truth in the fact that our for-profit banking system is simply not designed to handle that volume of consumer-friendly optimization. A casino whose slot machines paid out to every player wouldn’t stay in business very long, after all.

Other finance gurus have pointed to the fact that AI agents might simply go haywire, regardless of what they’ve been instructed to do.

“You’re assuming they’re going to act properly on your behalf and they may not,” JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon told a room full of economists and financial experts in Chicago earlier this month. “You can’t stop it. You just have to, like, manage the hell out of it.”

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: Oregon Police Are Charging a Local News Outlet $2.5M for Records About One Cop
items.content:
Two members of the Eugene, Oregon, Police Department in a photo posted to the department’s Facebook page on Aug. 26, 2026.   Screenshot: Eugene Police Department via Facebook

Lauren Harper is Freedom of the Press Foundation’s first Daniel Ellsberg Chair on Government Secrecy.

How much does it cost to get more information about a cop who punched someone in the face?

If you guessed anything lower than $2.5 million, you’d be wrong — at least according to the city of Eugene, Oregon.

In August, the local news outlet Double Sided Media filed a public records request for records about police officer Justin Peckels, which focused on potential misconduct between 2018 and 2026. Peckels has been the subject of community complaints, including for punching a resident in the face during a traffic stop, making the records vital for oversight and their release clearly in the public interest.

The city’s response is beyond belief. In its response to the request on Monday, the Eugene Police Department claimed searching for records and processing the request would take at least 44,816 hours of staff time and cost approximately $2,484,599.04. (A separate request by the outlet for similar records concerning a former police officer, Eric Klinko, was met with a comparatively modest estimate of $195,869.52 , for a grand total of nearly $2.7 million for both requests.)

The open invoice by the City of Eugene, Ore. dated Aug. 1, 2026, in response to Double Sided Media’s request for public records relating to a police officer accused of misconduct.   Screenshot: City of Eugene

“Once the City receives payment of $2,484,599.04 staff will continue processing your request,” the letter from the department’s public records division read. “If the actual cost of processing your request exceeds the amount you have paid the City, you will be required to pay the difference before the City will provide the records you have requested.”

Peckels’s file is either the largest in the world, or city officials have intentionally maintained their databases in such a way as to ensure fulfilling public records requests is prohibitively expensive. The city’s response points, at a minimum, to the latter. It justified the multimillion-dollar price tag by claiming it couldn’t narrow the custodians whose records it would need to search, despite the targeted nature of the request, and maintained it must search all records of all city employees, past and present.

By that logic, if someone ever worked in Eugene’s parks and recreation department, their records could contain responsive information about police misconduct, and must be manually pulled and reviewed, one by one.

Google DeepMind Engineer Resigns in Protest of Pentagon Contract

Trump’s Obsession With Somalia Isn’t Just Racist. It’s Been Lethal.

Corporations Are The Real Healthcare Fraudsters, Inspector General Report Shows

This goes far beyond incompetence. It’s an intentional effort to make a response artificially voluminous — and cost prohibitive — to intimidate the journalist into dropping it entirely.

Normally, agencies are required to search the specific custodians most likely to possess responsive records, not every groundskeeper or clerk on the city payroll. If the city were acting in good faith, officials would have asked Double Sided Media to help them identify the most likely record-holders, not take it upon themselves to cast a citywide dragnet as its first step.

What makes Eugene’s money-grab particularly galling is its technology double standard. While it apparently can’t invest in efficient search software, the police department recently signed a two-year $342,000 contract for nearly 60 AI-powered Flock automated license plate readers. This project was so secretive that the ACLU of Oregon had to sue the city for records about how the cameras were being used and demonstrates, among other inclinations, the city’s eagerness to employ sophisticated software to deploy against residents.

items.title: A vision for a next-generation timeline
items.content:
The timeline is the most interacted-with piece of any chat software. It's where messages live! It's hard to have a chat app without one.

Unfortunately, the matrix protocol has... compromises... in the timeline made for the sake of federation. From the incosistent ordering between sync and history on Synapse, to the inability to jump to pinned messages from before you joined, to the mystery of what happens when you join a room your server previously left.

The good news is we have a solution! The bad news is it's gonna take a while. This talk is a rundown of every step needed to get a next-generation timeline. I'll explain stitched ordering, timeline fragments, and why we need state DAGs.

items.title: What's wrong with AI? (explaining AI skepticism)
items.content:
This is a rant. It is not intended to profoundly change your mind. If you think AI is great, great: go and play with your thing. Yes, I know it is surprisingly good and quite cool and impressive, and you can now do things you couldn’t do before (although you’re not actually doing anything). I don’t care. I’m not going to justify my opinions or back up my claims. I’m writing this for two audiences - the doubtors and the sceptics. I don’t want to initiate a debate. If you disagree with anything, please don’t tell me. I’m happy to provide more detail on my thoughts if you ask - but don’t use that to disguise a disagreement or the start of a discussion.

For the doubters, those who have qualms, niggling doubts, fears that are hard to put words to, or are simply out of their depth understanding what’s happening: I want to make your worries concrete, put them into words, and give reassurance that they are reasonable and proportionate. I also want to give you other things to worry about, in the hope of turning you into a sceptic.

For the sceptics, those who either see some use for AI but reject how it is being pushed on us now, or are wholehearted horrified by the whole thing, I want to offer reassurance that you’re not alone, and list out all the things you’re worried about. I’m quite sure the current climate is making you feel like you’re in a madhouse, and having your thoughts set out with some kind of structure might at the very least release your mind to focus on other things. That is what it has done for me.

I learned to write computer programs ( code ) in the 8-bit home computer revolution in the UK in the 1980s, and have been coding ever since, for fun and for profit. I studied computer science at university, did a Masters in software engineering, worked in proto-social-media in 1999, then film special effects. I returned to university to do a second Masters in Bioinformatics, learning biochemistry and computational methods for analysing biochemical data, and then I did a PhD and postdoctoral research in computational molecular biology, modelling biological molecules and publishing a couple of papers. I dabbled in some computational art projects, and then worked in an EU project for collecting, standardising and analysing data on cancer and other disease treatment, for scientists to sift through and discover what works best. Finally I moved to work for a very famous music software company, where I’ve been ever since, creating tools for hundreds of very famous people, and hundreds of thousands of others, to make music.

Normally I would give this biography only as context of where I’m coming from, rather than to lend weight to my words. However, for the purpose of this essay, I’m absolutely stating all this to impress you. I know what I’m talking about, I’ve lived through several computing revolutions, from before mobile phones and the internet-of-the-masses, through to today, and all that time been actively interested in and interestedly active in making computers do things, and thinking about what computers should do. I have, for most of this time, been a technology booster, and if I’d been inclined to start a business, might have become one of the hateful tech bros imposing their vacuous philosophies on our lives.

I am lucky, in a way, that my first job out of university was for a company that collected personal data and used psychological research it to create an addictive social media website - years before social media took off. Already, then, I saw how vulnerable we are to relatively simple tricks. I was creating them. It felt bad, as many of our users were my friends (mostly also software engineers), and I could directly see everything they did on our website. It felt wrong, it was wrong, so I left.

All of this means, you should listen to me. I know what I’m talking about, I have a background of analysing and solving problems, I know more-or-less how this stuff works, I have a history of working for and supporting…
items.title_ko: AI의 무엇이 문제인가? (AI 회의론 설명)
items.summary_ko: 글쓴이는 AI에 대한 자신의 회의적 시각을 정리한 글을 썼다고 밝힌다. 이 글은 의견을 바꾸려는 논증이라기보다, AI에 대해 막연한 의구심을 가진 사람들과 AI 도입 방식에 반대하거나 강하게 우려하는 회의론자들을 대상으로 한다. AI가 뛰어난 기술이라는 점은 인정하면서도, 독자들의 걱정을 구체적으로 말로 옮기는 것이 목적이다.
items.content_ko: 이 글은 일종의 푸념이며, 독자의 생각을 크게 바꾸려는 글이 아니다. 글쓴이는 AI가 놀랍도록 좋고 인상적이며 이전에는 할 수 없던 일을 가능하게 한다는 점을 인정한다. 다만 자신의 의견을 정당화하거나 주장을 뒷받침하지 않겠다고 밝힌다. 글의 대상은 두 부류다. 첫째는 막연한 걱정이나 설명하기 어려운 두려움을 가졌거나, AI가 어떻게 돌아가는지 잘 이해하지 못하는 의구심 있는 사람들이다. 글쓴이는 이들의 걱정을 구체적인 말로 옮기고, 그런 걱정이 합리적이고 적절하다는 점을 알리고 싶다고 한다. 둘째는 AI를 일부 쓸모 있다고 보면서도 지금의 도입 방식을 받아들이지 않는 회의론자들, 혹은 AI 전반에 크게 충격을 받은 사람들이다. 글쓴이는 이들에게 고려할 만한 다른 걱정거리도 제시해 회의적인 시각을 더 굳히고 싶다고 말한다. 글쓴이는 토론을 시작하려는 것이 아니므로, 동의하지 않는 부분이 있더라도 굳이 알리지 말아 달라고 요청한다.

items.title: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library
items.content:
Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library is dedicated to inspiring a love of reading by gifting books free of charge to children from birth to age five, through funding shared by Dolly Parton and local community partners in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia and Republic of Ireland.

Inspired by her father’s inability to read and write Dolly started her  Imagination Library in 1995 for the children within her home county. Today, her program spans five countries and gifts millions of free books each month to children around the world.

“When I was growing up in the hills of East Tennessee, I knew my dreams would come true. I know there are children in your community with their own dreams. They dream of becoming a doctor or an inventor or a minister. Who knows, maybe there is a little girl whose dream is to be a writer and singer.

The seeds of these dreams are often found in books and the seeds you help plant in your community can grow across the world.”

In 1995, Dolly Parton launched an exciting new effort,  Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library , to benefit the children of her home county in East Tennessee, USA. Dolly’s vision was to foster a love of reading among her county’s preschool children and their families by providing them with the gift of a specially selected book each month.

By mailing high quality, age-appropriate books directly to their homes, she wanted children to be excited about books and to feel the magic that books can create. Moreover, she could ensure that every child would have books, regardless of their family’s income

There is simply no limit on how far we can take this program and to what ends of the earth, but it is an absolute impossibility without your help. If your community or a community that you are aware of doesn’t yet offer this proven early childhood literacy program, then we challenge you to Get Involved! It’s actually quite easy to bring the Imagination Library to life in your community and we have an onslaught of available resources to help you Start A Program including a personal trainer which we like to call “Regional and State Directors” So come on, you can do it, follow this link to get a simple checklist of what you need to do to Get Onboard Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library.

items.title: Building Java ME Apps with Modern Tooling
items.content:
Java ME (Micro Edition, also referred to as J2ME) is a platform for running Java applications on small resource constrained devices, such as feature phones from before the iPhone era. It is largely considered a dead platform with the advent of smartphones, and modern feature phones such as KaiOS use web technologies instead for their apps.

However it is likely that you or someone you know have one of these old phones lying around, and you may be interested in how you can make Java apps that will run on it. This post goes through how to build a simple Java ME app solely with modern tooling in a modern environment, without needing anything from the old Sun Java ME SDKs.

The instructions in this blog post assume a Linux-y terminal environment, but you could also follow along with Git Bash or a similar environment on Windows.

Here is a simple Hello World MIDlet that we will use. It will show a simple form using the LCDUI API with the text “Hello World!”:

We will compile this with javac , but we first need the stub JARs from MicroEmulator available in the lib directory. Extract cldcapi11.jar and midpapi20.jar and put them in a lib directory next to the src directory.

The cldcapi11.jar provides the CLDC 1.1 API and midpapi20.jar provides the MIDP 2.0 API . MIDP 2.0 is circa 2002, and is probably what you want to use for widest compatibility, while it has some important features that MIDP 1.0 lacks.

Then we can compile the Java source file with the following command:

(To compile multiple .java files in src , you would put $(find src -name "*.java") instead.)

MIDlets need some metadata in the META-INF manifest file to work. Most of the fields are self-explanatory:

For the MIDlet-1 field, the format is a comma-separated list of three values: The human-readable name of the MIDlet, the path to the icon inside of the JAR, and the fully qualified class name of the entrypoint class. Since the above Java code specifies no package, it will be in the default package at the root of the JAR.

Save this to resources/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF , creating a resources/ directory to house assets to put in the final JAR. Also put a 16x16 PNG icon in resources/icon.png . Then let’s package everything together into a JAR:

Now we have a JAR file build/input.jar … But we need to preverify it before it can be run on a Java ME device.

Preverification is a process required for the KVM (the minimal Java virtual machine used in Java ME) to ensure that the bytecode is valid. Traditionally this would be done by a preverify tool from the original Java ME SDK, but ProGuard supports doing the same thing and is more modern.

You can also use ProGuard to shrink, optimise and obfuscate your code to reduce the footprint of the resulting JAR, which is especially important for Java ME apps where the JAR size limit can be very strict. But for this example we disable all of that for now and just specify -microedition to do the preverification.

Now you have a app.jar file that can actually be run on a Java ME device or in an emulator. You can use MicroEmulator to run it, or something with more features like FreeJ2ME-plus , currently the best J2ME emulator for desktop platforms.

Now that you have gotten it running in an emulator it would be nice to get it running on the real hardware. The feature phone I had lying around that’s the most functional is the Sony Ericsson S312, a budget feature phone from 2009. It even has a camera!

Java feature phones tend to have connectivity and storage mediums that are generally considered obsolete nowadays. My Sony Ericsson S312 has a proprietary charger cable with no USB on either end - supposedly you can use a special USB transfer cable, but that was a separate accessory that doesn’t seem worthwhile to obtain. In addition to this, the physical external memory storage is some strange card format that is distinct from any standard kind of SD card (M2 memory stick, not to be confused with the M.2 connector).

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: The Commentapocalypse Is Nigher – Random Thoughts
items.content:
Allowing comments on a WordPress blog is only viable if you have a spam checker. Fortunately Automattic (the people behind WordPress) also provide (free) access to Akismet antispam. Because if you run a WordPress blog, you will be getting hundreds of spam comments per day:

Nobody can wade through all of that, but Akismet correctly identifies all of this junk, so you never actually see it. Thanks, Automattic!

But ever since LLMs became a thing, I’ve assumed that comment spammers would be using them to post reasonable-sounding comments that would bypass Akismet… and there have been instances of this, but the deluge took longer to arrive than expected. But it seems to have started for real now:

This first wave of AI spam is easy enough to identify — they all vaguely agree with something you said in the blog post, and then link to some shady, scammy AI video thing. And Akismet doesn’t identify these for some reason or other. I mean, even though you can’t determine that it’s spam based on the comment itself, the URLs should be a good enough indicator, right?

C’mon, Akismet — you can do it! I have faith in you!

Heh, while writing this blog post, I got the following comment (correctly identified as spam by Akismet). Amusing, but not LLM spam.

I’m dreading the next wave of LLM spam, though — this initial wave is pretty stupid, but the next wave will have better text and no links (to make you approve the comment), and then the next comment will be automatically approved (as per standard WordPress settings), and that is the one that will have the links to the spam site.

So I guess you should flip your comments setting to “Comment must be manually approved”:

This future is so annoying, man. No flying cars except fake flying cars, and all of this junk we have to deal with.

items.summary_ko: WordPress 블로그는 스팸 필터 없이는 댓글을 허용하기 어렵고, 지금까지는 Akismet이 스팸을 거의 완벽하게 걸러 왔다. 그러나 LLM으로 그럴듯한 댓글을 쓰는 AI 스팸이 본격적으로 등장했다. 이들은 글 내용에 맞장구치는 댓글을 달고 수상한 AI 영상 사이트 링크를 붙이는데, Akismet이 이를 잡아내지 못하고 있다는 내용이다.
items.content_ko: WordPress 블로그에서 댓글을 허용하려면 스팸 필터가 반드시 필요하다. 다행히 WordPress를 만든 Automattic이 무료로 Akismet 스팸 필터를 제공한다. 블로그를 운영하면 하루에도 수백 개의 스팸 댓글이 들어오는데, Akismet은 이를 정확히 걸러내 글쓴이가 이런 스팸을 직접 보지 않도록 해 준다. 글쓴이는 LLM이 등장한 뒤로 스팸 댓글 작성자들이 LLM으로 그럴듯한 댓글을 만들어 Akismet을 우회할 것이라고 예상해 왔다. 실제로 그런 사례가 있었지만, 대량의 공격은 생각보다 늦게 왔다. 이제 본격적인 흐름이 시작된 것으로 보인다. 첫 번째 물결의 AI 스팸은 식별하기 쉽다. 블로그 글에 대체로 동의하는 댓글을 달고, 수상한 AI 영상 서비스 링크를 붙이는 식이다. 그런데 Akismet은 이를 잡아내지 못한다. 글쓴이는 댓글 내용만으로 스팸임을 판단하기 어렵더라도 링크만 봐도 충분히 걸러낼 수 있어야 한다고 말한다. 글을 쓰는 도중 글쓴이도 스팸으로 분류되어야 할 댓글을 받았다고 한다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-115825 📢 Source: CPANSec 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False HTTP::Server::PSGI versions before 1.0056 for Perl allow a single request to crash the server by declaring a large Content-Length. The request body is read with sysread() calls sized by the remaining Content-Length. Perl grows the read buffer to the requested length before any data arrives, so the server tries to allocate as much memory as the client declares. A remote attacker can send one request with a large Content-Length and a few body bytes, and perl exits with an out-of-memory error before the application is called. HTTP::Server::PSGI runs as a single process, so the server stays down until restarted. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-25T16:51:54.897Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-115825

This workshop founded in 1882 still makes dried bonito like they did back in the Edo period .

How katsuobushi — Japanese dried bonito, said to be the world’s hardest food — is made in Nishi-Izu, Japan. Inside Kanesa Katsuobushi Shoten, a workshop founded in 1882, 5th-generation craftsman Yasuhisa Serizawa still uses the 200-year-old “tebiyama” hand-fired smoke-drying method that only a few workshops in Japan preserve. Watch fresh bonito being filleted and boiled for 90 minutes, smoke-dried more than 10 times over a hand-tended wood fire, repaired with bonito paste, fermented with koji mold and sun-dried for months — over half a year until the fish becomes as hard as wood and shines like a jewel. From fresh catch to katsuobushi.

Check out Kanesa Katsuobushi Shoten’s website for more info; here’s what they say about the tebiyama drying/smoking method (Google translation):

This method of making dried bonito flakes has been used in the Tago district of West Izu for a long time, and its history is said to date back about 300 years (to the Edo period). It involves digging a vertical hole about 2 meters deep, burning firewood (raw wood from Izu: oak, sawtooth oak, cherry, etc.) from the bottom of the hole, and smoking and drying the dried bonito flakes with the high temperature of an open flame. This method is called the Tebiyama-shiki smoking method. It is the oldest existing smoking method, and only a few bonito flake manufacturers in the country continue to use this method to make dried bonito flakes, so it is said to be a legendary method. The Tebiyama-shiki smoking method is said to produce dried bonito flakes with a rich flavor because the surface of the bonito is smoked all at once with the high temperature of an open flame, locking in the umami.

items.title: When a glibc update accidentally breaks Chromium's audio (2021)
items.content:
A few weeks ago, I merged in a pull request to update the Chromium Flatpak to use runtime

version 21.08. I had given it some testing without running into any issues, plus the

binary-compiled Chromium variants like Chrome, Brave, and Edge were all already on runtime

21.08, thus it seemed like an easy merge. What could go wrong?

Then, the next morning, I woke up to see a PR filed to

that the update broke video playback , with some errors about the "audio renderer".

First off, I tried it out myself and confirmed that YouTube was completely broken. This

didn’t show up in testing because I almost never use YouTube on desktop, preferring the

mobile app instead, so I failed to observe any issues with it.

The last several lines are definitely not from Chromium itself, as they don’t follow the

standard Chromium log format. A quick google of the error pointed me to

this Gentoo issue , detailing that the error is actually

being logged by glibc. It included this code fragment from within the glibc source code:

For some context: futex is a Linux syscall that’s used in various synchronization

operations, such as mutexes and condition variables. In this case, when futex is run, an

unexpected error code is returned, causing glibc to panic. The chance of the kernel

returning a brand-new type of error due to a Flatpak runtime upgrade is…​not very high,

to say the least. But, how else would another error code end up being returned here?

Well, it turns out, there’s one important thing that stands between glibc and the

Chromium’s sandboxing architecture on Linux is an

multi-level system , where the first layer restricts the process’s runtime environment,

and the second layer restricts the process’s syscall access. That second layer is known as

the BPF sandbox : if a syscall is executed that is not explicitly allowed, the BPF

sandbox rejects it, returning a custom error code. Syscalls…​syscalls like futex, right?

At this point, I recalled a previous experience I had with Chromium’s sandboxing while

working on the Flatpak port: the audio service sandbox , which is what applies the BPF

sandbox to the audio process. Given that the errors in the screenshot showed a connection

to the audio renderer, this seemed like a useful target. With this in mind, I was able to

grab a core dump from the crashing audio service and retrieved this traceback:

Note the bottom few frames, which refer to code inside PulseAudio’s client library,

libpulse. This essentially confirmed that the error was indeed from the audio service.

Given my previous experience with said service, I recalled that there was a

flag controlling whether or not the audio sandbox was enabled, so I decided to try

disabling it to confirm it was actually the issue, via

--disable-features=AudioServiceSandbox . It did indeed stop the audio service from

crashing. (Unfortunately, videos still did not play, but that later turned out to be due

to unrelated network connection issues.)

But, why was this only broken on Chromium, and not Chrome or Brave? Well, Chromium and its

which are essentially randomized feature flag controls to perform A/B testing and gradual

rollouts. When I checked the active feature trials in the various browsers via

chrome://version/?show-variations-cmd , it became apparent that only Chromium had the

AudioServiceSandboxLinux feature trial active, among many, many other trials (this part

is important later!). By contrast, Chrome, Brave, and Edge had no reported issues tied to

YouTube, and this field trial was not active there.

Chromium’s audio service is crashing due to an unexpected error returned from futex .

This only occurs when the audio service sandbox is enabled.

items.title: Code and Cake - Docker is weird
items.content:
I decided to make my own container runtime for fun, and even though I’m still early on, I’ve learned that Docker is weird . Here’s some weird things I learned about Docker.

Unlike VMs, containers are just processes with special restrictions on them. Your kernel is still running that process! And if you know where to look, you can even find that process in /proc.

There’s not really a linux feature that’s just “containers” either. Instead, containers are really 5 different linux kernel features in trenchcoat.

Namespaces hide what the host and container can see, cgroups limit container resource usage, and there’s a whole bunch of networking magic I don’t understand that lets you isolate a container’s network.

Images are just folders that Docker puts somewhere and then calls chroot (or pivot_root ) to make that folder your container process’s new root directory. So if you run docker run -it --rm ubuntu /bin/bash , Docker is going to:

Docker’s container runtime, runc , is written in Go, and Go has some design choices that make it less suited for a container runtime. Go’s runtime is natively multi-threaded. That’s a really cool feature, but it leads to some challenges in runc .

Many of the Linux syscalls a container runtime needs to make have to be done in a single-threaded environment, so runc has a crazy C module that runs before Go’s runtime initializes so it can run those syscalls.

Go also doesn’t have fork! Fork only forks the main thread, so it’s kind of a footgun in a runtime like Go’s. But a container runtime really wants to fork, set up a bunch of restrictions, and then exec the process you actually put in docker run . To get around this, runc execs /proc/self/exe with a special command line arguement that identifies it as a child process to approximate a fork.

This is pretty easy to miss if you, like me, run Docker in MacOS. Many of the Linux kernel APIs that container runtimes use require, or at least used to, to be run as root, so the Docker daemon usually runs as root. I can only imagine that container security is a very tough job.

This seems better these days. The big exception seems to be networking. If you’re running a rootless container runtime, it looks like it has to reimplement the whole networking stack in userspace to actually give you the same features!

I’ve only just started my own container runtime, and I already feel like I’ve learned so much about Docker. Writing your own version of a tool you use is a great way to learn about it!

items.content_ko: 작성자는 컨테이너 런타임을 직접 만들어 보면서 Docker가 이상하다는 것을 알게 되었다고 밝혔습니다. 컨테이너는 VM과 달리 특정 제약이 걸린 프로세스일 뿐이며, 호스트 커널이 그 프로세스를 그대로 실행하고 있어 /proc에서 찾을 수 있습니다. '컨테이너'라는 단일 리눅스 기능은 없으며, 실제로는 다섯 가지 리눅스 커널 기능이 합쳐진 것입니다. 네임스페이스는 호스트와 컨테이너가 서로 보는 범위를 숨기고, cgroups는 자원 사용량을 제한하며, 네트워크 관련 기능으로 컨테이너의 네트워크를 격리합니다. 이미지는 Docker가 어딘가에 두는 폴더일 뿐이고, chroot나 pivot_root를 호출해 그 폴더를 컨테이너 프로세스의 새 루트 디렉터리로 만듭니다. items.title: AI use leads UC Berkeley math professor to see 'no point' in grading homework
items.content:
Richard Borcherds, a UC Berkeley professor and Fields medalist, no longer grades his students’ homework. After seeing how many of his students used AI to consistently receive top scores, he felt there was “no point” in paying readers to grade for correctness in homework, as AI use is now unavoidable.

Prolific student AI use and advancements in AI technology leaves the future of mathematics uncertain.

Richard Borcherds, a UC Berkeley professor and Fields medalist, no longer grades his students’ homework.

After seeing how many of his students used AI to consistently receive top scores, he felt there was “no point” in paying readers to grade for correctness in homework, as AI use is now unavoidable.

Borcherds revealed this in a sit-down interview Tuesday, following OpenAI’s announcement that AI agents apparently solved one of mathematics’ most difficult unsolved problems, the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem.

“If AI continues to improve at present rate, then, in a few years, there’ll be nothing human mathematicians can do that AI can’t do better,” Borcherds said.

Borcherds said he currently grades on completion if a student hands in their homework. He admitted that it is “not a very good system,” but at the moment, he has no alternative.

Borcherds stated he no longer knows whether to encourage students to go into the math department , as it seemed five years ago that being a mathematician was one of the safest careers from the AI boom.

“I have no idea what to advise. I even asked ChatGPT this exact question, and even ChatGPT said it didn’t have any idea what was going to happen,” Borcherds said.

He described a plentiful amount of “inertia” in the academic system and said he wouldn’t be surprised if things stayed the same in the math department for a couple years despite AI developments.

He drew a comparison to physical paper journals, which publish even though they have been “utterly pointless” for two decades.

“There have been plenty of technical breakthroughs in the past — hand weaving was put out of business by looms, and horses were put out of business by motor cars, and so on,” Borcherds said. “This is the first time anything like this has happened in mathematics, though.”

The Berkeley Division of the Academic Senate asks that faculty include a statement about course expectations including the use of AI tools for coursework in course syllabi, according to an email from Anne Marie Richard,  assistant vice provost for undergraduate education and chief academic technology officer.  However, she said the direct policies on AI use can vary dramatically with course level and focus area .

Campus has tried several AI detection tools, including Turnitin and Rumi , but have determined that these tools aren’t adequate enough to be standardized on campus.

AI policy for classes is up to the discretion of faculty, but there is a growing database of sample AI use statements available in the AI Hub, the campus directory for AI tools, training and policies, for faculty to use in their syllabi, according to Richard.

items.title: Balloting has completed for C++26. Unfortunately it was Disapproved
items.content:
P-Members voting: 12 in favor out of 20 = 60 % (requirement >= 66.66%)

(P-Members having abstained are not counted in this vote.)

Member bodies voting: 9 negative votes out of 22 = 41 % (requirement <= 25%)

Sort of a sad day for the C++ community. Hopefully we can heal and move on from this in a productive manner.

There were 12 countries that abstained. In several cases because they could not reach to a common position. That is another signal of a contested draft.

Please, note that before C++26 all other standards passed unanimously.

Why should this be a sad day for the C++ community? Taking into account the number of P-members who abstained due to a lack of consensus, which makes the NO vote even more significant, sinking such a flawed contracts proposal is a good sign of a healthy, engaged, and competent community at the national body level.

That some people were willing to put the entire C++26 standard at risk to push through such a controversial and deeply flawed proposal is, of course, concerning. Fortunately, the national bodies recognized the problem before it was too late.

And perhaps it is also a clear signal that WG21's 'experts in the room' voting approach needs to be reconsidered.

I assume this was not a complete surprise and that those who voted against it had voiced opposition or at least reservations previously? Is the most promising path forward to reduce the scope and try again? Or were there things excluded that people really wanted?

Such is the life of standards. Anything particular?

It is hard to heal after the decades of the same social issues reappearing. What lessons should we learn to be able to move on in a productive manner?

12 in favor out of 20 who did not abstain gets 8 voting against, but then we have 9 negative votes out of 22? Not that it matters terribly since it doesn't seem very close.

So sad to hear this, but indeed, let's learn from this, and regroup and move on.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title: AI bubble update: 79% of companies say their GPUs sit idle at least half the time, yet most plan new AI platforms
items.content:
Most surveyed companies running AI in production say the GPUs they use sit idle at least half the time, and most of those companies plan to add or switch AI compute platforms anyway, according to the latest data from VentureBeat Intelligence.

A whopping 79% of the 218 respondents who reported GPU utilization said their GPUs are busy half the time or less, across three monthly VB Pulse surveys from July through September . Among those companies, 70% said they plan to adopt a new, additional or replacement AI compute platform within the next 12 months. The share with idle GPUs held between 77% and 81% in each of the three months. We reported the September results Thursday ; the three months of data show the pattern holding steady.

Those numbers matter because Wall Street is arguing over whether AI is a bubble. On October 13, the International Monetary Fund warned that a sharp fall in AI share prices could threaten global financial stability . Most of that argument has focused on the companies selling AI compute, such as Nvidia, cloud giants Microsoft, Google and Amazon Web Services, and specialized GPU clouds like CoreWeave, and on whether they are building more capacity than their customers will pay for. We looked at what those customers are actually doing.

At first glance, the numbers look like a contradiction. Why would companies with so much unused GPU capacity plan to add or switch AI compute platforms? And why would they leave GPUs idle when, as technology leaders tell me, they are under heavy pressure in this fall's budget season to cut their AI bills?

The demand for AI is real, but it is landing in a different place than the idle GPUs. Professionals and consumers keep using more AI, and much of that work runs through the frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI. That demand will keep supporting those companies' spending on compute for some time. The mismatch sits one level down, inside enterprises that are paying for two kinds of AI that cannot easily stand in for each other.

The first kind is capacity. I believe many companies were scared by reports of GPU shortages in 2024 and 2025 and lined up GPU capacity so they would not be caught short. Much of the capacity companies use sits idle, our surveys show, though the surveys did not ask how companies got that capacity or whether they controlled it directly..

The second kind is frontier models. Engineers and other employees have preferred the most capable models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, paid by the token through those companies' APIs, through monthly subscriptions or through the big cloud providers. The thinking was that companies needed the best intelligence to race ahead, and they would sort out the economics later. Uber's chief technology officer, Praveen Neppalli Naga, said in August that "we're coming to the end of the so-called tokenmaxxing era," after Uber spent its 2026 AI budget within a few months, according to Fortune. An AI leader at a Fortune 500 company, speaking on background, told me in October that AI costs keep rising, and that while the company expects productivity gains to offset them eventually, it does not know that yet.

Amazon Web Services, Microsoft and Google now sell Anthropic's or OpenAI's models through their clouds, and OpenAI said on Wednesday that its models will reach Google Cloud in the coming weeks. OpenAI's frontier GPT models and Anthropic's Claude models are closed, so the cloud provider or the model maker runs them on its own infrastructure and bills by the token or for capacity reserved for that one model. A company cannot load them onto GPUs it already controls. To shift work onto those GPUs, a company has to switch to an open-weight model and run it itself. items.title_ko: AI 거품 논쟁: 기업 79%는 GPU를 절반 이상 놀리는데도 새 AI 플랫폼 도입을 계획
items.summary_ko: VentureBeat Intelligence의 최신 조사에 따르면, 프로덕션에서 AI를 운영하는 기업 대다수가 GPU를 최소 절반 이상 유휴 상태로 두고 있다. GPU 활용률을 응답한 218개 기업 중 79%가 가동 시간이 절반 이하라고 답했고, 이 중 70%는 향후 12개월 안에 새로운, 추가 또는 교체용 AI 컴퓨팅 플랫폼을 도입할 계획이라고 밝혔다. 이 비율은 3개월 조사 내내 77~81% 범위를 유지했다.
items.content_ko: 조사 대상 기업 대다수가 GPU를 절반 이상 쉬게 두고 있지만, 그럼에도 많은 기업이 AI 컴퓨팅 플랫폼을 추가하거나 바꿀 계획이라고 한다. 7월부터 9월까지 세 차례 진행된 VB Pulse 설문 결과가 근거다. 이 수치는 월가에서 AI가 거품인지를 두고 벌어지는 논쟁과 맞닿아 있다. IMF는 10월 13일 AI 주가의 급락이 글로벌 금융 안정을 위협할 수 있다고 경고했다. 이런 논쟁은 주로 Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, AWS, CoreWeave 같은 AI 컴퓨팅 공급업체에 초점이 맞춰져 있으며, 이들이 수요보다 많은 설비를 짓고 있는지가 쟁점이다. 본문은 중간에 끝난다.

items.title: There isn't an easy exploit for this PHP vulnerability
items.content:
I know, I know. It's all you're hearing about. That, and the number 4 .

Don't get me wrong, there's clearly a bug here and it really does matter. But this is not easy to exploit. It is certainly nowhere near as eay as Log4Shell/Heartbleed/RoRYaml etc.

EDIT: Putting this up here so people read it. You should patch your servers anyway. There is a real vulnerability here, but exploiting it is significantly harder than people are making it out to be - it is certainly not as easy as e.g. log4shell.

I don't think this PHP vulnerability is that exploitable. I think that 5 years ago people would've understood this, but now people are being deluded by their LLMs telling them they have an exploit when they don't.

If you take a look at github right now, there are thousands, literally thousands, of "PoC" exploits for this vulnerability. One thing you'll notice about all of them though, is that they do not work against a vanilla PHP instance.

Go ahead, stand up a php server you think is vulnerable in Docker and then run the PoC yourself . Don't get your LLM to do it. No. Run the script, yourself. The exploits don't work.

I think that a lot of people had assumed that LLMs will be able to build an exploit chain instantly from reading the diff, and that even if this was harder to exploit than other exploits, LLMs would've levelled the playing field. Well. There's no working exploit. Now what?

When I think about "we're very fucked" CVE10s on the Internet, I think of the following vulnerabilities:

RoR YAML decoding (send a post body with bad yaml in it)

Log4shell (set your user-agent to ${jdni:ldap:})

Shellshock (copy env x='() { :;}; echo vulnerable' and edit to taste)

Heartbleed (ask for Content-Length 10000000)

The second these vulnerabilities made the news, there were botnets doing the rounds causing damage. And this was before LLMs! People have to write the botnets. With their hands!

It's been 10 hours since this vulnerability has been posted, and half the software world is looking at it, and lord knows 100,000 people have got their "superintelligence" on the case. Nevertheless, there's no working exploit. The ones doing the rounds are fake, or only work in a lab, because...

Script kiddies (and script adults, who have also switched their brains off) now all think that, well, they don't understand UAF chaining, but this Claude guy knows everything and can totally make an exploit.

Hilariously, this results in the LLM giving their younger-brother an unplugged controller. It says exploit all across the screen... and has some smoking gun transcripts... but it's modified the server you're testing against to have a severe vulnerability. Cheating!!

https://github.com/david-alvarez-rosa/php-rce

https://github.com/eness/php2shell-CVE-2026-109618-CVE-2026-109619-PoC

I just plucked these three because they were the ones with the most stars, but it goes on for miles and miles.

One really amusing thing in common with most of these "PoC"s is that they lean on "LFI", or local-file-inclusion, to make the vulnerability. In non-php terms, their exploit chain requires the server to already have a severe code-level vulnerability.

It's not rare for PHP apps to be fucked in some sense, but requiring the server to have an existing vulnerability where users could cat /etc/password is an insane pre-requisite. If you need this, this does not make this a severe bug.

The strangest thing is that so many people have independently made this extraordinarily weird defect in judgement. That is because they haven't independently made this decision. Claude/Etc. has done all of the judgement for them, hence the bizarre distribution in logical errors.

There's something important to be said here about how many people have Claude/GPT make design decisions for them, and how AI is the primary decision maker in the world right now. You've got this bizarre case of "Decision Schelling Points" where a method of solving a problem is extremely overrepresented,…

items.title: 사생활침해 범죄가 의심 됩니다. 도움이 필요합니다
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-115823 📢 Source: CPANSec 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl send response bodies for HEAD requests, desynchronizing responses on keep-alive connections. For a HEAD request Starman omits chunked framing but still writes the body returned by the application, on both the array and streaming response paths. Responses with a 1xx, 204 or 304 status also carry the body. On a keep-alive or pipelined connection the client reads those bytes as the start of the next response. A front-end proxy that reuses upstream connections may then pair responses with the wrong requests. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-25T16:51:19.961Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-115823
